steps.hint: Start from zero and add the first frequency.
Add the second frequency to your total.
Add the last frequency; this total is n.

opener.label: Before any graphs

steps.pre: Which position is the exact middle? Position
steps.say: No maths yet, just look at the line. As many people should stand to the left of the middle person as to the right.
steps.hint: Count in from both ends until you meet: with 9 people the middle is the 5th.

steps.say: Now a bigger line: 80 people, shortest to tallest. The middle sits halfway along.
steps.hint: Halve the total number of people.

steps.say: You just found the median by its position, n ÷ 2. On a cumulative frequency graph you read across from that position. And counting people up as you move along the line is exactly cumulative frequency.

steps: Cumulative frequency: keep a running total; plot each total at the top of its class.
Median at n ÷ 2, Q1 at n ÷ 4, Q3 at 3n ÷ 4; read across the curve, then down.
Box plot shows min, Q1, median, Q3, max. IQR = Q3 − Q1, range = max − min.
Histogram: frequency density = frequency ÷ class width; frequency = area of the bar.
method_card.title: Cumulative Frequency, Box Plots & Histograms
method_card.content:
Cumulative frequency is a running total of frequencies, plotted at the upper class boundary. Read the median across from ½n, Q1 from ¼n and Q3 from ¾n.

A box plot shows min, Q1, median, Q3 and max. IQR = Q3 − Q1; range = max − min.

On a histogram, frequency density = frequency ÷ class width, and the area of each bar equals its frequency.

steps: When class widths differ, work out each bar's frequency separately as density × its own width, then add for the total.
Compare distributions from box plots using the median (average) and the IQR (spread).
An outlier lies more than 1.5 × IQR beyond a quartile: above Q3 + 1.5 IQR or below Q1 − 1.5 IQR.
gold.title: Gold: unequal widths, comparisons and outliers

example.question: Classes 0 to 20 (FD 1) and 20 to 30 (FD 4). Find the total frequency.

steps: Cumulative frequency is a running total: add each class frequency onto the last. The final total is n.
The median is at position n ÷ 2, the lower quartile Q1 at n ÷ 4, and the upper quartile Q3 at 3n ÷ 4.
From a box plot: IQR = Q3 − Q1 (the box width) and range = max − min (whisker to whisker).
bronze.title: Bronze: totals, positions and box plot spreads

example.question: Frequencies 5, 9, 6. Find the total cumulative frequency and the median position.

steps: Frequency density = frequency ÷ class width, so a bar's frequency is density × width (its area). The formula runs both ways.
Quartile positions still use n ÷ 4, n ÷ 2 and 3n ÷ 4, whatever the sample size.
To read a cumulative frequency curve: go up to the position, across to the curve, then down to the value.
silver.title: Silver: frequency density and reading a curve

example.question: A histogram bar spans 10 to 30 with frequency density 3. Find the frequency.

gold.hint: Frequency is density times width, and this class is 20 wide.
gold.display: Diagram not drawn accuratelyThe histogram has classes 0-10 (FD 1.2), 10-20 (FD 2.5) and 20-40 (FD 1.8). Find the frequency of the 20-40 class.

guided_steps.say: Frequency is the area of the bar: frequency density × class width. Mind the wider class.

guided_steps.hint: Top minus bottom of that class.
Multiply the density by 20, not by 10.

guided_steps.done: That returns the density 1.8, so the frequency 36 is right.
guided_steps.hint: Divide frequency by width to get density back.

misconceptions.message: That uses width 10. The class 20 to 40 is 20 wide, so frequency = 1.8 × 20 = 36.

gold.hint: Compare the median lines of the two boxes.
gold.display: Diagram not drawn accuratelyThe boxes show two data sets. A: Q1 = 15, median = 22, Q3 = 30. B: Q1 = 18, median = 25, Q3 = 32. Which has the higher median?

misconceptions.message: A has median 22 and B has median 25, so B has the higher median line.

gold.hint: Interquartile range is the upper quartile reading minus the lower quartile reading.
gold.display: A cumulative frequency graph has total 80. The median at position 40 reads 32, Q1 at position 20 reads 24, and Q3 at position 60 reads 42. Find the IQR.

guided_steps.say: The interquartile range is Q3 − Q1, using the values read off the curve, not the positions.

guided_steps.pre: Upper quartile read from the curve: Q3 =
Lower quartile read from the curve: Q1 =

guided_steps.done: That returns Q3, so the IQR of 18 is right.
guided_steps.hint: Add the IQR back onto Q1.

misconceptions.message: Those are the positions (60 and 20), not the readings. The IQR uses the values off the curve: 42 − 24 = 18.
That is Q3 − median. The IQR is Q3 − Q1 = 42 − 24 = 18.

gold.hint: Work out each bar as density times its own width, then add, watching the widths.
gold.display: Diagram not drawn accuratelyThe histogram has classes 0-5 (FD 4), 5-15 (FD 2) and 15-20 (FD 6). Find the total frequency.

guided_steps.say: Total frequency adds up every bar's area: frequency density × width for each class, then sum.

guided_steps.pre: Check by adding the areas again: 20 + 20 + 30 =
guided_steps.done: All three bar areas add to 70, so the total frequency is 70.
guided_steps.hint: Add the three areas once more.

misconceptions.message: That uses width 5 for every class. The middle class 5 to 15 is 10 wide: 4 × 5 + 2 × 10 + 6 × 5 = 70.

gold.hint: Add 1.5 times the interquartile range onto the upper quartile.
gold.display: An outlier is defined as more than 1.5 × IQR above Q3. Q3 = 45 and IQR = 20. Find the upper outlier boundary.

guided_steps.say: The upper outlier boundary is Q3 plus 1.5 lots of the IQR.

guided_steps.done: That returns 30 = 1.5 × IQR, so the boundary 75 is right.

misconceptions.message: That adds only one IQR. The rule uses 1.5 IQRs: 45 + 1.5 × 20 = 75.
That is just 1.5 × IQR. Add it onto Q3: 45 + 30 = 75.

bronze.hint: Add the frequencies of the first three classes only.
bronze.display: Frequencies: 4, 8, 12, 10, 5. Find the cumulative frequency after the 3rd class.

guided_steps.say: Cumulative frequency is a running total. Add the frequencies one class at a time up to the 3rd.

guided_steps.hint: Add the third frequency to your running total.

guided_steps.pre: Check by adding all three straight: 4 + 8 + 12 =
guided_steps.done: Same total, so the cumulative frequency after the 3rd class is 24.
guided_steps.hint: Add the three frequencies in one go.

misconceptions.message: That is the total of all five classes. The cumulative frequency after the 3rd class only adds the first three: 4 + 8 + 12 = 24.
That includes the 4th class. Stop after the 3rd: 4 + 8 + 12 = 24.

bronze.hint: The median position is the total divided by 2.
bronze.display: A cumulative frequency graph has a total frequency of 80. What cumulative frequency do you read across from to find the median?

guided_steps.say: The median sits at the middle of the data. For n values that middle position is n ÷ 2.

guided_steps.pre: How many values in total? n =
guided_steps.hint: Read the total frequency from the question.

guided_steps.pre: So you read across from a cumulative frequency of
guided_steps.done: At CF = 40 you read the median off the curve.
guided_steps.hint: It is the position you just found.

misconceptions.message: That is the lower quartile position (n ÷ 4). The median is halfway: n ÷ 2 = 80 ÷ 2 = 40.

bronze.hint: The lower quartile position is the total divided by 4.
bronze.display: A cumulative frequency graph has a total frequency of 60. What cumulative frequency do you read across from to find the lower quartile Q1?

guided_steps.say: The lower quartile Q1 sits a quarter of the way through the data: position n ÷ 4.

guided_steps.pre: So Q1 is read across from a cumulative frequency of
guided_steps.done: At CF = 15 you read Q1 off the curve.

misconceptions.message: That is the median position (n ÷ 2). Q1 is a quarter of the way in: n ÷ 4 = 60 ÷ 4 = 15.

bronze.hint: Interquartile range is the upper quartile minus the lower quartile.
bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accuratelyThe box plot shows min = 10, Q1 = 15, median = 20, Q3 = 28, max = 35. Find the interquartile range (IQR).

guided_steps.say: The interquartile range is the width of the box: Q3 − Q1.

guided_steps.pre: Read Q3, the right side of the box: Q3 =
guided_steps.hint: The right edge of the box.

guided_steps.pre: Read Q1, the left side of the box: Q1 =
guided_steps.hint: The left edge of the box.

guided_steps.done: That gives Q3 back, so the IQR of 13 is right.

misconceptions.message: That is the range (max − min). The IQR is the box width: Q3 − Q1 = 28 − 15 = 13.
That is Q3 − median. The IQR runs across the whole box: Q3 − Q1 = 28 − 15 = 13.

bronze.hint: Range is the largest value minus the smallest.
bronze.display: Diagram not drawn accuratelyThe box plot shows min = 10, Q1 = 15, median = 20, Q3 = 28, max = 35. Find the range.

guided_steps.say: The range is the full spread, from the lowest value to the highest: max − min.

guided_steps.pre: Read the maximum, the right whisker end: max =
guided_steps.hint: The far right of the whisker.

guided_steps.pre: Read the minimum, the left whisker end: min =
guided_steps.hint: The far left of the whisker.
Subtract the smallest from the largest.

guided_steps.pre: Check: 10 + 25 should return the maximum, so 10 + 25 =
guided_steps.done: That gives the maximum back, so the range of 25 is right.
guided_steps.hint: Add the range onto the minimum.

misconceptions.message: That is the interquartile range (Q3 − Q1). The range spans the whole data: max − min = 35 − 10 = 25.

bronze.hint: Frequency density is frequency divided by class width.
bronze.display: A histogram class runs 0 to 20 with frequency 10. Find the frequency density.

guided_steps.say: Frequency density spreads the frequency evenly across the class: frequency ÷ class width.

guided_steps.hint: Top of the class minus the bottom.
Divide the frequency by the width.

guided_steps.done: That returns the frequency, so the density 0.5 is right.
guided_steps.hint: Multiply width by density to get frequency back.

misconceptions.message: That is width ÷ frequency, upside down. Frequency density is frequency ÷ width = 10 ÷ 20 = 0.5.

bronze.hint: Add the heights of all four bars.
bronze.display: The frequency chart shows test scores. What is the total frequency?

guided_steps.say: The total frequency adds up the height of every bar.

guided_steps.pre: Check by adding all four straight: 5 + 12 + 18 + 10 =

misconceptions.message: That leaves out the last bar. All four bars count: 5 + 12 + 18 + 10 = 45.

bronze.display: Frequencies: 3, 7, 15, 10, 6. Find the total cumulative frequency.

guided_steps.say: The total cumulative frequency is every frequency added together.

guided_steps.hint: Add the last two frequencies to your running total.

guided_steps.pre: Check by adding all five straight: 3 + 7 + 15 + 10 + 6 =
guided_steps.done: Same total, so the final cumulative frequency is 41.

misconceptions.message: That stops before the last class. The total adds all five: 3 + 7 + 15 + 10 + 6 = 41.

silver.hint: Frequency density is frequency divided by class width.
silver.display: A histogram class runs 15 to 25 with frequency 20. Find the frequency density.

guided_steps.hint: Top minus bottom of the class.

guided_steps.done: That returns the frequency, so density 2 is right.

misconceptions.message: That is width ÷ frequency, inverted. Frequency density is frequency ÷ width = 20 ÷ 10 = 2.

silver.hint: Frequency is frequency density times class width.
silver.display: A histogram bar covers the class 0 to 5 with frequency density 3. Find the frequency.

guided_steps.say: On a histogram the frequency is the area of the bar: frequency density × class width.

guided_steps.hint: Top minus bottom of the class.

guided_steps.done: That returns the density, so the frequency 15 is right.
guided_steps.hint: Frequency divided by width gives density back.

misconceptions.message: That divides instead of multiplying. Frequency = density × width = 3 × 5 = 15.

silver.hint: The lower quartile position is n divided by 4.
silver.display: A cumulative frequency diagram has n = 100. At what position is the lower quartile Q1?

guided_steps.say: The lower quartile Q1 sits a quarter of the way through the data: position n ÷ 4.

guided_steps.pre: Check another way: a quarter of 100 =
guided_steps.done: A quarter of 100 is 25, so Q1 is at position 25.

misconceptions.message: That is the median position (n ÷ 2). Q1 is at n ÷ 4 = 100 ÷ 4 = 25.

silver.hint: Work out each interquartile range, Q3 minus Q1, then compare.
silver.display: Diagram not drawn accuratelyThe boxes show the middle 50% of two data sets. A: Q1 = 20, Q3 = 45. B: Q1 = 25, Q3 = 55. Which has the larger interquartile range?

misconceptions.message: A has IQR 45 − 20 = 25 and B has IQR 55 − 25 = 30, so B has the wider box.

silver.hint: Frequency is density times the class width, and the width here is 20.
silver.display: A histogram bar covers the class 10 to 30 (width 20) with frequency density 1.5. Find the frequency.

guided_steps.say: Frequency = frequency density × class width. The wide class needs its full width.

guided_steps.hint: Top minus bottom of the class.

guided_steps.done: That returns the density 1.5, so the frequency 30 is right.

misconceptions.message: That uses width 10. The class 10 to 30 is 20 wide, so frequency = 1.5 × 20 = 30.

silver.hint: Find the position n divided by 2, read across to the curve, then down to the score.
silver.display: The cumulative frequency diagram shows exam scores for 50 students. Estimate the median score.

guided_steps.say: The median is the middle value. Find its position, then read across the curve and down to the score.

guided_steps.pre: 50 students, so the median is at position 50 ÷ 2 =
Read across from cumulative frequency 25 to the curve, then down. The score is
guided_steps.hint: The curve reaches CF = 25 at a score of 20.

guided_steps.pre: Confirm: how many students scored 20 or less? Read the curve up at score 20:
guided_steps.done: Half of the 50 students (25) scored 20 or less, so 20 is the median.
guided_steps.hint: Read the cumulative frequency at score 20.

misconceptions.message: That is the cumulative frequency you read across from, not the score. Follow the curve down to the horizontal axis: the median score is 20.

silver.hint: Subtract the cumulative frequency at 20 from the cumulative frequency at 30.
silver.display: A cumulative frequency table reads: up to 10 = 8, up to 20 = 22, up to 30 = 40, up to 40 = 50. Find the frequency in the 20 to 30 class.

guided_steps.say: A cumulative frequency is a running total. The frequency IN a class is the jump in cumulative frequency across it.

guided_steps.hint: Read the total at the top of the class.
Read the total at the bottom of the class.
Subtract the lower running total from the higher.

guided_steps.pre: Check: 22 + 18 should give the total up to 30, so 22 + 18 =
guided_steps.done: That returns 40, so 18 is the frequency in the 20 to 30 class.
guided_steps.hint: Add the frequency back onto the earlier total.

misconceptions.message: That is the cumulative frequency up to 30, a running total. The frequency in the class is the jump: 40 − 22 = 18.
That is the 30 to 40 frequency. For 20 to 30 subtract the two totals either side: 40 − 22 = 18.

problem_bank.silver_description: Frequency density both ways, quartile positions for larger samples, and reading a cumulative frequency curve.
